adds.rationale: Oklo, a pure-play SMR fission developer, went public via SPAC on May 10 2024 and reports ~80% of inbound customer inquiries come from data-center operators — a direct in-window match to the profile's named next wave (SMR fission + PPAs to AI data centers) that the uranium-mining proxy CCJ does not capture.

removes.rationale: Cameco's Q1 2024 results confirm the uranium-mining leg is solid but mature and already broadly recognized (in line with guidance); at the 6-ticker cap this slot is better used on OKLO, a fresher buildup-phase name mapping precisely onto the profile's SMR/AI-data-center sub-thesis.

news_evidence.summary: Cameco Q1 2024 in line with outlook: adjusted net earnings $56M, adjusted EBITDA $345M, uranium segment earnings up 34% YoY — a steady consensus story, not a new catalyst

rationale_overall: One swap within the nuclear bucket: OKLO (freshly-listed SMR pure-play with dated AI-data-center demand evidence) replaces CCJ (mature, already-consensus uranium exposure), sharpening the fit to the profile's 'SMR fission + PPAs to AI data centers' next wave while holding at cap 6. The rest held: AI (MSFT, NVDA) remains the dominant riding wave with no crest (NVDA's split and ascent to most-valuable-company read as confirmation); ITA (defense) and RKLB (rockets, Neutron testing progressing) intact; IONQ (quantum) beat Q1 revenue guidance and raised bookings. Tanker names were declining off spring highs (poor entry). Result: MSFT, NVDA, ITA, RKLB, IONQ, OKLO.
